profile.reading: This is Verne Globals Helsinki area data center campus, known as The Air, at Mittalinja 1 in Vantaa, Finland, a genuine and distinct site from the companys better known flagship campus on a former NATO base near Keflavik, Iceland. The building, internally coded FL-HEL-DC01, was originally developed by Finnish operator Ficolo and became operational in 2019, running entirely on renewable wind power with a distinctive kinetic building facade that responds to airflow, waste heat from the site fed directly into the local district heating network, and backup generators running on renewable diesel reported to cut emissions by roughly 90 percent compared to conventional diesel backup. In February 2025, Verne announced the acquisition of adjacent land from Onvest, a Finnish family owned company, to add two further buildings for AI and high performance computing workloads using liquid cooling, expanding the campus toward four total buildings numbered DC01 through DC04 and describing the combined campus, existing plus planned expansion, at a target capacity of about 70 megawatts. Ficolo, the original developer of this Helsinki site, was acquired and folded into the Verne Global brand around 2022 by Digital 9 Infrastructure, the same period in which Digital 9 also acquired UK based Volta Data Centres, after having separately bought the original Verne Global platform for about 231 million pounds in 2021. French private equity firm Ardian then acquired the full Verne Global platform, including this Helsinki campus, the Iceland flagship site, and the former Volta UK assets, from Digital 9 Infrastructure in a deal announced November 27, 2023 and completed around March 2024, reported at a value of up to 575 million dollars. Verne markets the wider Helsinki campus as running on a claimed 100 percent renewable, low carbon power supply, positioning it alongside its Iceland flagship as one of the companys two Nordic renewable powered campuses.
